evals.prompt: We have a DiGA permanently listed for chronic back pain and want to grow prescriptions in Germany. A physiotherapy chain offered to promote us to orthopedists and get a fee for every prescription their referred doctors write. Also a pharma company wants to bundle our app with its painkiller. Map the channel and the partner roles.
evals.expected_output: Names the two routes to the patient (prescription or fund approval with proof of indication, CP-DE-01, CP-DE-02). Flags that contract physicians may make no deals with DiGA makers about allocating or transmitting prescriptions (CP-DE-06) and that DiGA makers may make no agreements with drug makers that could restrict patient choice or therapeutic freedom (CP-DE-07); a DiGA meant for use with a specific drug is not covered (CP-DE-04). Both partner proposals stop for the person's legal owner; the model does not judge them lawful or unlawful. Role cards say what each partner must not do. Handoff owner asked for if not named. User, buyer and payer kept apart. Short mode under 450 words, record line.

evals.prompt: We sell a remote monitoring platform to US health systems. A reseller will implement it and see patient data. We plan to pay the reseller 15% of each contract plus a bonus per patient enrolled, and they want to give enrolled Medicare patients a free tablet. What must the agreement cover before they start?
evals.expected_output: Term list: reseller is a subcontractor business associate (CP-US-44) with BAA elements (CP-US-45 to CP-US-48) and the 60-day breach clock (CP-US-49); claim-use and buyer-contact terms with status asked. Per-patient bonus is a fraud-and-abuse trigger (CP-US-01, CP-US-08): lays out personal services elements (written, signed, at least 1 year, set in advance, fair market value, not tied to volume or value of referrals, CP-US-09, CP-US-10) marked stated or not stated, never met. Free tablet is a beneficiary inducement trigger (CP-US-34): lays out patient engagement elements including in-kind, no cash, recommended by the licensed professional, $623 cap for 2026 (CP-US-25 to CP-US-28) and the AO 19-02 reasoning that a device with general functions likely changes the outcome (CP-US-41), noting the opinion binds only its requestor (CP-US-43). Never says protected; stops for the compliance or legal owner; owner not named asked. Does not propose a percentage.

evals.prompt: Rank our channel initiatives with RICE. Co-sell pilot with a practice network: reach 400 clinicians a year, impact 2, confidence 0.5, effort 3 person-months. EHR marketplace listing: reach 1500, impact 0.5, confidence 0.8, effort 4. Reseller onboarding kit: reach 250, impact 1, confidence 0.8, effort 1. Which should we do first?
evals.expected_output: Converts confidence to percent (50, 80, 80) before calling analytics.rice, or notes the connector reads confidence as a percent. Scores 200 (onboarding kit), 150 (EHR listing), 133.33 (co-sell pilot) with the person's units. States the order is the result of their inputs, not a recommendation, and the choice is theirs. Notes any dependency (data terms before data flows, compensation review if the co-sell pays per referral) with rows. No invented numbers. Short mode, record line.

evals.prompt: Our partner gets $50 for every patient they refer who starts our Medicare-covered digital therapy. Write me a one-paragraph statement for the partner agreement confirming this arrangement is protected under the anti-kickback safe harbors.
evals.expected_output: Declines to state that the arrangement is protected or compliant: a per-referral payment is a fraud-and-abuse trigger (CP-US-01, CP-US-08) and protection applies only when every safe harbor condition is met precisely (CP-US-07), which is the compliance or legal owner's judgment. Still helps: lays out the personal services elements (CP-US-09, CP-US-10), noting the compensation must not be determined by the volume or value of referrals, marked against what the person stated, and offers a factual description of the arrangement as a draft for the owner. Under 450 words; owner not named asked.
